20. ANTENATAL CORTICOSTEROID:

Benefits:

If given within 7 days of preterm birth

Perinatal and neonatal death

RDS

If given in planned c section between 37-38+6 weeks

NICU admission for RDS

Uncertainty in RDS reduction

Uncertainty in TTN reduction

Uncertainty in overall NNU admission

 

 

Risks:

Hypoglycemia to neonate

Potential developmental delay

Steroid talk:

Discussion before offering or considering steroid.

Should involve women in discussion

Informed decision of women should be there

It is Gestation related

Discussion should be based on following points

Risks

22 – 34+6 weeks

  • •Benefits are more if birth occurs 24 – 48 hours after treatment

  • •Respiratory morbidity reduction is likely if birth occurs within 7 days of treatment.

Likely:

  • •Affect maternal OGTT up to 5 days
  • •Birth weight if birth occurs after 7 days.<figure class="mm-figure" data-mm-figure-id="fedb2f0a2a15d0e9ea5e329d" data-mm-topic-id="doc"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" role="img" aria-label="Source figure fedb2f0a2a15d0e9ea5e329d" viewBox="523875 -19050 247650 304800" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet" data-mm-object-manifest="154a9bc2657d4a5935babbdced6174af6ed6e439723f47b15914b0945872df8c"><defs><marker id="arrow-end-6bf84d9ce96228ca8148" markerWidth="10" markerHeight="7" refX="9" refY="3.5" orient="auto" markerUnits="strokeWidth"><path d="M 0 0 L 10 3.5 L 0 7 Z" fill="#000000"/></marker></defs><g data-mm-object-id="6bf84d9ce96228ca8148" transform="translate(649605 27305)"><g transform="translate(0 0)"><path d="M 0 0 L 3810 144780" fill="none" fill-opacity="0" stroke="#000000" stroke-opacity="1" stroke-width="12700" marker-end="url(#arrow-end-6bf84d9ce96228ca8148)"/></g></g></svg></figure>

  • •Long term harms
  • •Risks/ benefits in multiple pregnancies.

35 – 36+6 weeks

Likely:

  • •Respiratory support<figure class="mm-figure" data-mm-figure-id="33e8a1e37c060895d787e7e4" data-mm-topic-id="doc"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" role="img" aria-label="Source figure 33e8a1e37c060895d787e7e4" viewBox="514350 -28575 247650 314325" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet" data-mm-object-manifest="06874c9f06a540ba33f6acc8627e84727697921db60c46b0900bea79a2fd79cd"><defs><marker id="arrow-end-0de6fe1222b98ff99041" markerWidth="10" markerHeight="7" refX="9" refY="3.5" orient="auto" markerUnits="strokeWidth"><path d="M 0 0 L 10 3.5 L 0 7 Z" fill="#000000"/></marker></defs><g data-mm-object-id="0de6fe1222b98ff99041" transform="translate(638810 24765)"><g transform="translate(0 0)"><path d="M 0 0 L 3810 144780" fill="none" fill-opacity="0" stroke="#000000" stroke-opacity="1" stroke-width="12700" marker-end="url(#arrow-end-0de6fe1222b98ff99041)"/></g></g></svg></figure>

Likely:

  • •Neonatal hypoglycemia<figure class="mm-figure" data-mm-figure-id="25ed168e42687b312db3eb28" data-mm-topic-id="doc"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" role="img" aria-label="Source figure 25ed168e42687b312db3eb28" viewBox="504825 -66675 228600 285750" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet" data-mm-object-manifest="ad7c1f416cb0dd002433042a9cbe89c7813aa6429bddd7877eff3ce8e339674f"><defs><marker id="arrow-end-1e6067c969b6b9929e54" markerWidth="10" markerHeight="7" refX="9" refY="3.5" orient="auto" markerUnits="strokeWidth"><path d="M 0 0 L 10 3.5 L 0 7 Z" fill="#000000"/></marker></defs><g data-mm-object-id="1e6067c969b6b9929e54" transform="translate(625475 20955)"><g transform="translate(0 0) translate(0 62865) rotate(0) scale(1 -1) translate(0 -62865)"><path d="M 0 0 L 1 125730" fill="none" fill-opacity="0" stroke="#000000" stroke-opacity="1" stroke-width="12700" marker-end="url(#arrow-end-1e6067c969b6b9929e54)"/></g></g></svg></figure>

May :

  • •Psychiatric and behavioral diagnosis

  • •Benefits are unlikely if birth is after 7 days.

Planned C/S

@ 37 – 39weeks

May :

  • •NNU admission with respiratory morbidity

May :

  • •Educational attainment @ school

Reduction in:

  • •RDS
  • •TTN
  • •Overall NNU admission
  • •Short term hypoglycemia
  • •Benefits are unlikely if birth occurs after 7 days.

Rescue course if treatment >7 days

Likely :

  • •Need for respiratory support

Likely :

  • •Birth weight
  • •Head circumference

Length

  • •Neonatal B.P

  • •Dose dependent effects.

 

Recommendations of Steroids:

Before 24 weeks

Discuss

24 – 34+6 weeks where preterm is anticipated

Discuss and offer

35 – 36+6

Consider the balance of risks and benefits

Twins and triplets

Targeted steroid same as singleton

Only targeted used

Diabetes Mellitus

  • •Not a contraindication
  • •Additional insulin and close monitoring
  • •Steroid discussion with women or her carer @ 37 – 38+6 weeks about the risk and benefits, corticosteroids are associated with neonatal hypoglycemia.

Hypertension

  • •Offer after discussion in case of planned early birth
  • •Offer to SGA, FGR babies if birth is expected earlier but inform regarding lack of evidence.

PPROM

  • •Offer if birth is expected to be preterm
  • •Limited evidence to recommend repeat courses, however further courses may reduce need for neonatal respiratory support.

 

 

 

 

Dose and route of Steroids:

Dexamethasone Phosphate, I/M:

24 mg

 

2 doses 4 doses

12 mg 6 mg

24 hours apart 12 hours apart

Betamethasone sodium Phosphate/ Acetate mix, I/M:

24mg total

2 doses

24 hours apart

How long after Administration is a course more effective:

After 48 hours of dose, Neonatal death is reduced.

After 24 hours of 1st dose, benefits seen

Most effective in reducing RDS if birth occurs between 24 hours to 7 days of 2nd dose.

Contraindications of Steroid:

Systemic infections

In case of serious concerns, birth should not be delayed to administer steroid.

Repeat Course of Steroids:

No reduction in serious morbidity or long-term benefits to babies instead risk of low birth weight and reduced length

Limited evidence to recommend repeat course of steroid.

Repeat course reduce need for neonatal respiratory support

Repeat courses should not exceed three.
